title: TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours Draw Rules: Eligible Work, Time Bands and Conversion to Block Hours
content:
## A. What may be drawn

A.1 A work session on TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours is drawn only for a kind of work listed among the block's eligible kinds of work. Project work is drawn only where the block size allows time-and-materials project work, and only under a time-and-materials statement of work, never under a fixed-fee one.

A.2 Work that the client's ClearPath agreement already includes, hardware, licences and monthly fees are never drawn from a block.

A.3 Hours may be drawn only from a block whose status is active. This is the state shown on the block's own record when the draw is posted.

## B. Clauses of the standard conversion

B.1 *Minutes.* "Worked minutes are the recorded minutes rounded up to the billing increment and never less than the remote minimum for a remote session or the onsite minimum for an onsite visit." **This clause is no longer in force** for a remote session, a service visit, an installation visit, or a group of time-and-materials project time of a client holding exactly one live time-and-materials engagement; each of those draws now takes its minutes from the current rule for that kind of draw. The project time of a client holding no such engagement or two or more of them keeps this clause, wholly and line by line, its recorded minutes rounded up to the billing increment.

B.2 *Time band.* "The time band is holiday on weekends and observed holidays, emergency for work dispatched outside business hours at the client's request to restore a down system, after-hours for other work outside business hours on business days (the business days excluding the observed holidays), and business hours otherwise; only one band applies to a session, in that order of precedence." **This clause is no longer in force** for the draws listed in B.1; every other draw, the project time of a client holding no such engagement or two or more of them included, keeps it.

B.3 *Conversion.* "Converted block hours equal worked minutes divided by 60, times the resource ratio (technician, senior engineer or architect ratio), times the band multiplier (holiday, emergency or after-hours multiplier, and 1 in business hours), rounded half up to the hundredth of an hour." **This clause is no longer in force** for the draws listed in B.1; every other draw, the project time of a client holding no such engagement or two or more of them included, keeps it.

B.4 *Travel.* "Each onsite visit additionally draws the onsite trip hours as a separate travel entry at the business hours band with no ratio applied." **This clause is no longer in force**: travel to the client's site drawn from a block is now figured under the current travel rule.

## C. Worked case under B.1 to B.3 (hypothetical project line kept under the standard conversion)

A senior engineer logs 50 minutes on a weekday evening outside business hours on a TimeBank 40-Hour Block (15-minute increment, senior engineer ratio 1.25, after-hours multiplier 1.5). The minutes round up to 60; the band is after-hours; 60 divided by 60, times 1.25, times 1.5, gives 1.875, rounded half up to 1.88 block hours.

superseded_clauses: Worked minutes are the recorded minutes rounded up to billing_increment_minutes and never less than minimum_draw_minutes_remote for a remote session or minimum_draw_minutes_onsite for an onsite visit.

The time band is holiday on weekends and observed holidays, emergency for work dispatched outside business hours at the client's request to restore a down system, after_hours for other work outside business_hours_start to business_hours_end on business days (business_hours_days, excluding the observed_holiday_list), and business_hours otherwise; only one band applies to a session, in that order of precedence.

Converted block hours equal worked minutes divided by 60, times the resource ratio (technician_ratio, senior_engineer_ratio or architect_ratio), times the band multiplier (holiday_multiplier, emergency_multiplier or after_hours_multiplier, and 1 in business hours), rounded half up to draw_rounding_hours.
Each onsite visit additionally draws onsite_trip_hours as a separate travel row at the business hours band with no ratio applied.
